name: Stacked bar (absolute composition)
reader_question: How large is each total, and how is it divided among a few components of the same measure?
relationship: Part-to-whole in absolute units: components of one additive measure add to a stated total per bar.
use_when: Components are the same measure and genuinely additive
The absolute size of each total matters as much as its mix
avoid_when: Components are unlike instruments or statuses that must not be added — use status-separated-capital
Only the mix matters and totals differ widely — use percent-stacked
More than four components or six bars — use a table or ranked-bar

data_contract.notes: Measure and unit, one for every component
One value per component; bar totals are derived

units: One additive unit; the axis starts at zero and is hidden, with a bar-end total instead.

editable: Stacked bar chart with embedded workbook (Edit Data)
not_data_bound: Bar-end totals and the omitted-label note are positioned text computed from the fixture; editing chart data does not update them
Segment labels below the threshold are hidden by a number-format condition, not deleted

table_alternative: A table of rows by component with a total column, for exact lookup of every segment.
limitations: Only the bottom component shares a baseline, so inner segments are hard to compare across bars
Narrow segments are unlabelled and must be read from the table alternative

excluded_alternatives.reason: Splits one comparison across several shapes and defeats comparing totals
Statuses are not additive; status-separated-capital keeps them apart
